# Innovation Section — Template

Document type: Section template
Use: Structural guidance for writing the innovation section of a grant application.
Replace all [PLACEHOLDER] markers with real, verified information before use.

---

## Structure

A strong innovation section follows this order:

1. The problem and why current solutions fail
2. Your specific advance beyond the current state of the art
3. Evidence of novelty and freedom to operate
4. TRL progression

---

## Template

### What is the innovation?

[COMPANY NAME] is developing [BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF TECHNOLOGY OR SOLUTION] capable of [SPECIFIC PERFORMANCE TARGET WITH UNIT] — a [QUANTIFIED IMPROVEMENT]% [improvement/reduction/increase] on [CURRENT BENCHMARK].

The core innovation is [SPECIFIC TECHNICAL ADVANCE — be precise, one or two sentences].

[DESCRIBE THE SPECIFIC PROBLEM WITH CURRENT SOLUTIONS — what fails, degrades, costs too much, or doesn't exist].

The project will advance the technology from TRL [START TRL] ([describe current state]) to TRL [END TRL] ([describe target state]).

### Why is this beyond the current state of the art?

Existing solutions ([NAME KEY COMPETITORS OR EXISTING APPROACHES]) [describe their specific limitations with evidence]. [ACADEMIC OR INDUSTRY REFERENCE, year] has identified [SPECIFIC PROBLEM] but no commercial solution exists [at scale / at this cost point / with this performance].

Our approach differs by [SPECIFIC TECHNICAL DIFFERENTIATOR — what is new about your method, material, process, or combination].

[DESCRIBE FREEDOM TO OPERATE: patent searches completed, any IP filed or planned, any licensing arrangements].

---

## Writing guidance for this section

**Open with the performance target, not with your company.** Assessors read many applications — lead with the specific claim that makes your innovation worth funding.

**Name the existing solutions you are going beyond.** Saying "existing solutions are inadequate" scores lower than naming Competitor A, Competitor B, and explaining precisely what their limitations are.

**Quantify the advance.** "Significantly better" scores 1. "40% lower cost at equivalent cycle life" scores 3–4.

**State TRL precisely.** TRL 4 means laboratory prototype validated. TRL 7 means prototype demonstrated in operational environment. Use the correct definitions — assessors know them.

**Cite your state of the art sources.** Academic papers, industry reports, competitor datasheets. No source = assertion = low score.

---

## Section checklist before submission

- [ ] Current state of the art described with named examples
- [ ] Specific limitation of current solutions explained
- [ ] Our advance described precisely — not vaguely
- [ ] Improvement quantified with a number
- [ ] TRL start and end stated with definitions
- [ ] At least one source cited for state of the art claims
- [ ] Freedom to operate addressed
- [ ] Word count within limit
